Senses.PreferredTarget: pull the patchwork quilt over one’s head
AlternateTargets: cover one’s head with the monk’s quilt
the patchwork quilt drawn over the head
Senses.Note: Four deployments span four independent works.

Occurrences.Kwic: 又曰：衲被蒙頭萬事休，此時山僧都不會。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X82/X82n1571.xml). Complete Five Lamps (Vols. 34–120). Yunfeng Miaogao says that with the patchwork quilt over his head all matters stop and he understands nothing.

Occurrences.Kwic: 且道：無賓主話，火爐頭如何舉得？還委悉麼？衲被蒙頭萬事休，此時山僧都不會。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X68/X68n1318.xml). Continued Essentials from the Sayings of Ancient Worthies. Yuanwu Keqin caps his question about raising the guestless-hostless saying at the hearth with the covered-quilt line.

Occurrences.Kwic: 莫是衲被蒙頭萬事休此時山僧都不會得麼
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (L/L155/L155n1643.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Hongjue Min. Hongjue Min tests whether covering the head and letting all matters rest escapes the three bindings, without accepting it as sufficient. Canonical roster link: Muchen Daomin.

Occurrences.Kwic: 此去深山學逸叟，逢人罵徹始，任他千佛出人間，衲被蒙頭不知有。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J26/J26nB177.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Poshan. Poshan’s farewell verse tells the departing practitioner to cover his head with the quilt and remain uninvolved even if a thousand Buddhas appear.

ActorAttribution.GrammarEvidence: The book title and poem heading 送彼岸禪人住山 identify Poshan as the author of the exact headword-bearing verse.

Senses.Explanation: To pull the patchwork quilt over one’s head is to withdraw completely from claims, schemes, and public business. Chan masters use monastic bedding as an image of radical non-involvement: ten thousand matters stop, even claims to understand are set aside. Yunfeng joins the covered head to letting all matters rest; Yuanwu quotes the same line when asking how to raise the guestless-hostless saying at the hearth; Hongjue includes it among proposed escapes from mental binding and rejects treating it as an automatic solution; and Poshan’s farewell verse sends a practitioner into the mountains with the quilt over his head even if a thousand Buddhas appear.
